absent: Sleeping and locking constraints of optional subsystem statistic handlers beyond the held online reference.
Exact ordering and formatting of combined processor accounting output when subsystem detail is present.
Internal creation, polling, destruction and restart behavior of stall triggers and their worker.
Signal delivery path and permission checks beyond number validation and forwarding.
Task-level freezing transitions and descendant frozen count maintenance.
Resource statistics flush and snapshot lock implementation and nesting rules.
Filesystem node lifetime, notification delivery and timer rearming semantics.
Tree iteration guarantees under concurrent group creation, removal or migration.
Meaning of threaded versus non-threaded grouping beyond the termination restriction.
Computation of visibility and hierarchy filtering for default versus legacy schemas.

findings.text: Rendering helper for processor accounting of a group, callable from outside this file, producing usage and split time values plus an optional core scheduling line.
External control to request or clear freezing of a subtree, applying the change through descendants and emitting a completion notification when nothing further changes.
External helper to make a group file visible or hidden by safely acquiring its filesystem node reference.
External registration interface for control file schemas, supporting plain addition, default-only addition, legacy-only addition, and removal with rollback on failure.
External signal delivery entry that rejects invalid signal numbers and forwards valid requests toward per-process delivery.
Processor accounting file handlers that combine generic time output with scheduler subsystem detail, separating aggregate and local views.
Stall information file handlers mapping each resource class to its monitor, with write installing a trigger, poll waiting on it, and release tearing it down.
Lifecycle control files where one boolean toggles freezing of a subtree and a separate write-only trigger terminates member processes in eligible groups.

Generic file operations that establish per-open context with namespace reference, enforce delegation policy, and route reads and writes to type-specific handlers, with a timer callback forwarding expiry to file notification.
Frozen time reporting reflects accumulated frozen duration plus the currently open freezing interval when the freezing indicator is set, observed under a retry loop for consistency.
Subsystem state acquisition returns a usable online reference or nothing, never a stale offline reference.
Optional subsystem statistics are silent successes when the subsystem offers no handler or its state is unavailable, otherwise the handler result is propagated and the reference released.
Non-root groups report previously collected statistics after flushing and adjustment under protection, while the root group aggregates live per-processor counters across all processors.
Root aggregation folds interactive and background processor categories into user and system totals and preserves pleasant time separately, accumulating execution totals from both.
A descendant is effectively frozen when its own request or its parent effective state demands it, and subtrees with no change in effective state are skipped during propagation.
Termination walks live descendants and signals only user threads that are not already dying, broadening iteration to include threaded members.
Signal sending rejects out-of-range numbers before attempting delivery, and distinguishes privileged from unprivileged origin for accounting.
Writes from inside a delegated namespace to the namespace root are denied except for explicitly delegatable types.
Control schemas cannot be registered twice, select single or sequential handling from their capabilities, and fully unwind partial registration on failure.
Frozen time and flag updates are performed under interrupt-disabled set protection with sequence counting, allowing lock-free readers to retry on concurrent change.
Subtree freezing, termination, and control schema changes require the central group mutex held by the caller.
Subsystem state lookup for statistics is done under read-side critical section with online reference acquisition before release.
Base time snapshots are taken under the resource statistics lock after flushing, and file visibility changes acquire the per-file interrupt-disabled lock to obtain a stable node.
Pressure trigger installation and control writes hold a live reference on the group, temporarily releasing it only to create a polling worker and revalidating context before publishing.

Group freezer state carries request and effective flags, accumulated and start timestamps with a sequence counter, plus descendant freeze counts; base accounting carries execution, user, system, pleasant and optional idle totals.

Per-open context holds a namespace reference and an optional stall trigger; control type descriptors carry naming, delegation and hierarchy flags, subsystem binding, operation vectors, and optional write limits.
Two operation tables share open, release, write and poll handling with page-sized atomic writes, differing in that only the sequential variant offers iteration callbacks.
Freezing moves from idle to requested to effective across a subtree, accumulating time on transitions and revisiting empty or already settled groups to converge completion.

Stall monitoring toggles between disabled and enabled with per-resource files shown or hidden accordingly, and each open file moves from empty to armed to released for its single trigger, with the current enablement reported as a numeric flag.

Control schemas progress from initialized to linked to applied, with removal unlinking then withdrawing files and clearing state; opens allocate context and releases always drop the namespace reference.
Publishing a stall trigger after recreating a polling worker must recheck that the open context still exists, otherwise the new trigger must be discarded to avoid use after free.
Rightmost descendant search must avoid backward links that are unsafe under read-side protection, and freezing plus termination must skip kernel threads and already dying tasks.
Process-directed termination is rejected in threaded groups, and schema application touches only visible states while activation occurs solely on successful addition.
Statistic label frozen_usec denotes frozen duration in microseconds.
Processor accounting labels usage_usec and user_usec and system_usec and nice_usec denote total and split times in microseconds.
Label core_sched.force_idle_usec denotes forced idle time in microseconds where supported.
Freeze and stall enable controls accept zero for off and one for on, while the termination control accepts only one.
Control files advertise page-sized atomic write length by default, with per-type override permitted via duplicated operations.
Missing groups report device or entry absence, duplicate triggers report busy, threaded termination reports not supported, and out-of-range values report range error.
